precepts.text: The nation is called to gather itself together and seek the Most High before the day of his anger.
precepts.point: The prophets came together to accomplish a common mission. The work of the house does not get done unless the prophets and the people gather and labor together.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

precepts.why:
The house of God had been hindered for roughly two years when Haggai and Zechariah prophesied to the Jews, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose up to build, “and with them were the prophets of God helping them.” The prophets and the people came together for one common mission, and that is the call of Zephaniah: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.”

The gathering must happen “Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.” The nation is told to gather itself and “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.”

The work of the house does not get done unless the prophets and the people gather and labor together, and the nation is to gather and seek the Most High before the day of his anger.

precepts.text: Jacob calls his sons to gather together so they may hear what shall befall them in the last days.
precepts.point: The prophets came together to accomplish a common mission. The work of the house does not get done unless the prophets and the people gather and labor together.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

precepts.why:
Jacob gathered his sons the same way the prophets gathered the builders: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days. Gather yourselves together, and hear, ye sons of Jacob; and hearken unto Israel your father.”

The sons of Jacob had to gather to hear what should befall them in the last days. In Ezra 5 the prophets Haggai and Zechariah gathered the leaders, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose up with the prophets of God helping them. The pattern is the same: Israel gathers together, hears, and then the work gets done.

precepts.text: Assyria carried Israel away captive because they had sinned against the Most High their God.
precepts.point: They confessed that the fathers provoked the God of heaven, who delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and carried them to Babylon. This captivity is read in Second Kings, where Assyria took Israel and later Babylon took Judah.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

precepts.why:
The elders confessed to Tatnai that “our fathers had provoked the God of heaven unto wrath”, so he gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed the house and carried the people into Babylon. The captivity is read in Second Kings. First Assyria took Israel: “In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.”

And the reason is given: “For so it was, that the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, which had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods.” Israel went into Assyria for sinning against the Most High and fearing other gods; later Babylon took Judah for the same provoking. That is the history behind the elders' answer: they were the servants of the God of heaven and earth, rebuilding the house that a great king of Israel had built, after their fathers had provoked him and been carried away.

points: After the work had been hindered for roughly two years, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah stirred up the leaders, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose again to build the house of God.
The prophets came together to accomplish a common mission. The work of the house does not get done unless the prophets and the people gather and labor together.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: Tatnai the governor and his companions challenged the elders, demanding who commanded them to build the house and the wall.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: The eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, so the adversaries could not force the work to stop while a letter went to Darius.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: The elders answered plainly that they are servants of the God of heaven and earth rebuilding a house a great king of Israel had built long before.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: They confessed that the fathers provoked the God of heaven, who delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and carried them to Babylon. This captivity is read in Second Kings, where Assyria took Israel and later Babylon took Judah.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: Cyrus is called king of Babylon because he conquered Babylon and took possession of all it held, though he reigned out of Persia. He restored the gold and silver vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple.

note.label: Ezra 5: The Prophets Rise Up To Build

points: The letter asks Darius to search the king's treasure house to confirm that Cyrus made a decree to build the house of God at Jerusalem. The heathen always keep records on the children of Israel, so the matter had to be proven from the rolls.
